definition_zh: 非典型的；不寻常的；反常的
definition_en: not typical or usual; different from what is normal for a person, group, or thing
core_image: 一面整齐的瓷砖墙上，偏偏有一块颜色不对——就是它让人停下来看
scene: 医生把胶片挂上灯箱，笔尖停在角落一小块阴影上。The doctor pointed out one atypical cell among thousands of ordinary ones.
sceneCN: 这里 atypical 指「非典型的、不像平常的」（第 1 个义项：偏离常态）；句意：医生在成千上万个普通细胞中指出了一个非典型的细胞。画面里有灯箱、胶片和一支笔。

pos.zh: 非典型的；不寻常的；反常的

derivatives.zh: 典型的（去否定前缀后的基词）

senses.title: Not what is usual
senses.titleCN: 非典型的：不像平常那样
senses.definition: not showing what is typical or expected for a kind of thing
senses.definitionCN: 不表现某类事物通常或预期特征的
senses.example: Snow in June is atypical weather for this region.
senses.exampleCN: 六月下雪对这个地区来说是不合常理的天气。
senses.why: The prefix a- comes from Greek and simply negates the base; whatever typical covers, atypical pushes outside.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 来自希腊语，作用就是否定基词：typical 圈住的范围，atypical 都把它推出去。

senses.title: Unusual for a person
senses.definition: different from the way a particular person usually behaves
senses.definitionCN: 与某个人的惯常表现不同的
senses.example: He was quiet and polite, an atypical evening for the usually loud boy.
senses.exampleCN: 他安静又有礼貌，对这个平时吵闹的男孩来说，这个晚上很反常。
senses.why: The negation first attaches to the norm of an individual: what breaks the personal pattern is atypical.
senses.whyCN: 这个否定先落在个人的常态上：打破个人一贯模式的，就是 atypical。

senses.title: Medically irregular
senses.definition: of a disease or symptom, not presenting in the usual clinical form
senses.definitionCN: （疾病或症状）不以通常临床形式表现的
senses.example: The patient had atypical symptoms, so the diagnosis was delayed.
senses.exampleCN: 病人症状不典型，所以诊断被推迟了。
senses.why: Medicine is built on pattern recognition; a case that escapes the textbook pattern gets the negated adjective.
senses.whyCN: 医学建立在模式识别上；逃出教科书模式的病例，就冠上这个带否定的形容词。

senses.title: Not representative
senses.definition: not serving as a fair example of a whole group
senses.definitionCN: 不能作为整类事物的公正样本的
senses.example: The journalists warned that one village is an atypical sample of the country.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们提醒说，一个村子不能作为全国的典型样本。
senses.why: When a sample cannot stand for the group, the negation marks the gap between part and whole.
senses.whyCN: 当样本撑不起整类时，否定词就标出部分与整体之间的落差。

senses.title: Strikingly odd
senses.definition: so far outside the usual that it draws attention
senses.definitionCN: 偏离常态之远，以致引人注目的
senses.example: Her atypical courage surprised everyone at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她异乎寻常的勇气让会上所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: Deviation is neutral, but language leans on the visible: the further from the norm, the more the word points.
senses.whyCN: 偏离本是中性的，但语言偏爱可见的东西：离常态越远，这个词指向性越强。

senses.title: Atypical cells
senses.definition: of cells, showing abnormal structure that may signal disease
senses.definitionCN: （细胞）结构异常、可能提示病变的
senses.example: The biopsy found slightly atypical cells that needed watching.
senses.exampleCN: 活检发现少量非典型细胞，需要观察。
senses.why: Pathology borrowed the everyday negation and fixed it to form: cells that no longer look like their neighbors.
senses.whyCN: 病理学借走日常的否定词，把它固定在形态上：不再长得像邻居的细胞。

senses.title: Seasonally off
senses.definition: not matching the usual weather or season
senses.definitionCN: 与通常气候或季节不相符的
senses.example: An atypical warmth let the garden bloom in December.
senses.exampleCN: 反常的暖和让花园在十二月就开了花。
senses.why: Nature supplies the most legible norms, seasons; break a season and everyone sees the negation at work.
senses.whyCN: 自然提供了最清晰的常态——季节；季节一乱，谁都看得出这个否定词在起作用。

senses.title: Statistically out of line
senses.definition: of data, falling outside the expected distribution
senses.example: One atypical data point was checked twice before being kept.
senses.exampleCN: 一个异常数据点被核对两次后才保留。
senses.why: Statistics turns typical into a number; the negated word names whatever the number leaves out.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把「典型」变成一个数字；这个带否定的词命名一切被数字排除在外的东西。

intro.en: Atypical is a young word built from old parts: a Greek negative prefix fastened to a root meaning mark and pattern, through Latin and late Latin.
intro.cn: atypical 是个用旧料拼成的新词：希腊否定前缀，经拉丁语与晚期拉丁语的「印记、模式」一词，接在希腊词根上。

items.en: The root *teuk- meant to beat or strike; its later descendants came to name the mark made by a stamp or image.
items.cn: 词根 *teuk- 意为「敲打」；其后裔后来转指印章或图像敲打出来的痕迹。

items.en: typos meant blow, mark, image, and came to mean the figure one expects, the pattern of a kind.
items.cn: 希腊语 typos 意为「敲击、印记、图像」，继而指一类事物应有的图形，即模式。

items.en: typicalis, meaning symbolic, carried the Greek stem into scholarly Latin.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 typicalis「象征性的」把希腊词干带进学术拉丁语。

items.en: a- before a consonant is the Greek negative prefix, the same as in atom, originally uncuttable.
items.cn: a-（辅音前）是希腊语的否定前缀，与 atom「不可切分」中的 a- 同一。

items.en: Typical settled in English in the seventeenth century; atypical appears from the mid-nineteenth century, first in scientific writing.
items.cn: typical 于 17 世纪在英语中定型；atypical 自 19 世纪中叶出现，最早见于科学文献。

items.en: Medicine and statistics made atypical a technical favorite, while everyday use keeps the plain sense of not usual.
items.cn: 医学与统计学让 atypical 成为技术常用词，日常用法保留了「不寻常」的朴素义。

note.en: Group one collects the typical family and the negated forms; group two gathers words about what departs from the norm.
note.cn: 第一组收 typical 词族与否定形式；第二组收与「偏离常态」相关的词。

entries.definition: having the usual qualities of a group; the word atypical negates it.
entries.definitionCN: 典型的；有某类事物通常特征的，正是 atypical 所否定的基词。

entries.definition: usually; in a way that shows the normal pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 通常；以显示常态的方式。

entries.definition: the quality of being not typical, used in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 非典型性，用于技术文献。

entries.definition: in a way that is not usual or expected.
the first model of something, from the same Greek typos.
entries.definitionCN: 原型；初版模型，同出希腊语 typos。

entries.definition: not happening or done often; different from the ordinary.
deviating from the general rule, often used of data and findings.
entries.definitionCN: 异常的；不合规则的，多用于数据与研究。

entries.definition: different from what is normal, especially in a medical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不正常的，尤用于医学语境。

entries.definition: not following the usual pattern of time, form, or rule.
unusual because unusually good; atypical is neutral, this word praises.
entries.definitionCN: 例外的；因特别好而罕见的，atypical 中性，此词带褒义。

normalIntro.en: a- means not, typical means of the pattern; the word is a small equation you can read aloud.
normalIntro.cn: a- 意为「不」，typical 意为「典型的」；这个词本身就是一道可以读出声的小等式。

normal.en: atypical equals a plus typical: not typical, that is all.
normal.cn: atypical = a + typical：不典型，就这么直白。

normal.en: Compare atom: both use the Greek a- meaning not.
normal.cn: 对比 atom：两者都用希腊语 a-，义为「不」。

normal.en: Atypical pneumonia is famous because the disease hides from the textbook.
normal.cn: atypical pneumonia 出名，正是因为这种病躲开了教科书。

normal.en: Un- is the Germanic negative, a- the Greek one: unusual, atypical.
normal.cn: un- 是日耳曼否定前缀，a- 是希腊的：unusual 对 atypical。

normal.en: The stress lands on the old root of the mark and the pattern.
normal.cn: 重音落在「印记、模式」的老词根上。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of identical tiles with one tile turned the wrong color.
abstract.cn: 想象一墙完全相同的瓷砖，偏偏一块颜色不对。

abstract.en: The small a- is a tiny door out of the big room of the normal.
abstract.cn: 小小的 a- 是一扇小门，通向「常态」大房间之外。

abstract.en: Atypical is the word you reach for when the pattern breaks and everyone stares.
abstract.cn: 模式一破、众人侧目之时，就是伸手去取 atypical 之时。

examples.en: It is atypical for him to lose his temper in public.
examples.cn: 他在公共场合发脾气，这很不像他。

examples.en: The study excluded atypical samples from the final count.
examples.cn: 研究把非典型样本从最终统计中剔除了。

examples.en: Doctors watched the atypical cells carefully over the next year.
examples.cn: 此后一年，医生们密切观察那些非典型细胞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶！太噼口？」——诶，这个病例太不符合典型，噼里啪啦都对不上口

root: 希腊否定前缀 a-（不）+ typical（典型的）← 希腊语 typos「敲痕、印记、模式」；字面即「不属于模式的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one move: take the pattern, then cross it out, in weather, in a person, in a clinic, in a dataset.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个动作展开：先立常态，再把它划掉——在天气里、在人身上、在诊室里、在数据里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one tile in a neat wall that has the wrong color.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面整齐的墙上，偏偏一块瓷砖颜色不对。

branches.en: OUT OF THE USUAL: anything that breaks the ordinary course, from snow in June to a warm December.
branches.cn: 出离寻常：从六月飞雪到十二月返暖，一切打破常规的事物。

branches.en: ODD FOR SOMEONE: behavior that departs so far from one's own pattern that others notice.
branches.cn: 对某人反常：偏离自身模式之远，以致旁人察觉。

branches.en: THE CLINIC LOOK: symptoms and cells that do not match the textbook form.
branches.cn: 临床之相：不合教科书形态的症状与细胞。

branches.en: THE SAMPLE TRAP: a case that cannot fairly stand for its group.
branches.cn: 样本陷阱：不能公正代表整类的个例。

branches.en: THE NUMBER LEAVES: data points outside the expected distribution.
branches.cn: 数字之外：落在预期分布之外的数据点。

intro.en: atypical splits into the Greek negative a- plus typical, whose root typos means mark and pattern; the family adds adverbs, an abstract noun, and cousins like prototype.
intro.cn: atypical 可拆为希腊否定前缀 a- 加 typical，其词根 typos 意为印记与模式；词族还包括副词、抽象名词及 prototype 等同根词。

latinIntro.en: The Greek stem reached English through Late Latin typicalis; Latin kept the sense of image and figure.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词干经晚期拉丁语 typicalis 进入英语；拉丁语保留了图像与图形之义。

items.meaning: the state of not being typical
items.example: The atypicality of the data raised questions.
items.exampleCN: 数据的非典型性引起了疑问。

items.meaning: the first model of a kind
items.example: a prototype of the new car
the archetype of the tragic hero
